focus_details.name: Macerich

key_dates.note: Watch: SNO pipeline conversion, Forever 21 re-leasing progress
Term loan refinancing — watch spread vs SOFR

thesis_points: Quality over speed: replacing Forever 21 vacancies (~570K sqft) with experiential anchors at >2x legacy rents
New CEO Jackson Hsieh (ex-Spirit Realty) reduced ND/EBITDA from 10.8x → 7.8x within ~1 year of taking office
Crabtree acquisition: fortress-quality asset at $219/SF vs $261/SF peer, 11% going-in cap rate vs ~7-8% peers
Portfolio moat: 42 Class A malls in prime coastal metros (CA, NY, AZ, NJ, PA), $894/SF go-forward tenant sales
16 consecutive quarters of positive leasing spreads; SNO pipeline $90–140M+; new leases 9% above renewals
Deleveraging roadmap: $6.6B → ~$4.5B debt by 2029–2030, targeting ~6x ND/EBITDA via asset sales

key_debate.street: High leverage (8.2x vs SPG 5.7x, SKT 5.4x), tenant bankruptcies (Forever 21, Claire's) signal structural decline
key_debate.our_view: Occupancy gap is deliberate — quality tenants commanding >2x prior rents. Deleveraging credibly underway with $395M B/C sales in 2025

46,328 towers across 13 countries; 1.8 tenants/tower domestic (vs CCI 2.4x EU 2.1x) = significant colocation runway

overview.narrative:
REITs broadly retreated Monday with seven of eight subsectors in the red, dragged lower by rising long-end yields and renewed hawkish Fed commentary. Office was the clear laggard at -2.00%, led by HPP's -6.17% plunge on reports of further San Francisco lease terminations, while FSP shed -5.06% in sympathy. Towers fell -1.43% as duration sensitivity weighed on the group, with SBAC off -2.00%. Hospitality was the lone bright spot at +0.76%, with INN surging +1.80% and DRH climbing +1.59% on strengthening summer RevPAR data and renewed takeover chatter.

The standout intraday divergence was Industrial, where LXP ripped +4.00%—likely on portfolio repositioning headlines—while ILPT cratered -3.16%, underscoring the haves-versus-have-nots dynamic in leveraged industrial names. Healthcare showed a similar split, with WELL grinding higher +0.65% on defensive flows while STRW dropped -2.12%. The retail tape was surprisingly resilient given the rate backdrop, with CBL managing +0.51% even as MAC slid -1.27%.

Positioning into Tuesday favors a barbell approach: lean into hospitality momentum and high-quality defensive names like WELL while staying underweight rate-sensitive towers and troubled office. Watch the 10-year closely—a move above 4.60% could accelerate the selling pressure across leveraged balance sheets, particularly in office and net lease where NTST's -2.16% decline may signal further pain ahead.
